data.title: Middle East Eye: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cast doubt about reports of an "imminent threat" from Iran on Washington.
Speaking to reporters in the Philippines, Rubio said that US authorities routinely check for potential threats against the country, but added that most intelligence leads are not considered credible.
When asked if he was concerned about a possible attack on Washington, he said: "I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat.
"The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. And we have threat streams every day, and the majority of them are not credible. We have to follow up on them," Rubio added.
Rubio also questioned the credibility of sources cited in a CNN report about an alleged Iranian plot targeting the US capital, saying: "Some of your intelligence sources are liars; others are liars and criminals."
"I won't even comment on it because I don't know who's leaking this stuff to you guys. But they're either showboats and liars, or probably criminals if they're saying anything that's even half true."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Thirty years after Rabin's assassination, Israel is again flirting with political violence
data.author: Lubna Masarwa

Submitted by
Lubna Masarwa
on

In the wake of elections that handed Arabs the balance of power, we are witnessing an unprecedented outpouring of hate speech and racism
Benjamin Netanyahu, then the Israeli opposition leader, addresses the Knesset in September 1993, two years before the assassination of Yitzhak Rabin (Menahem Kahana/AFP)
Off
A week before the recent Israeli elections, I took my 10-year-old nephew to a cinema in West Jerusalem. As we got into a lift in the car park, a young Israeli Jew entered holding an M16 rifle. Other Israeli Jews got in too.
When we got out on the cinema level, my nephew said with a smile: “I’ll give you 100 shekels if you dare to speak Arabic in the lift.”
Speaking Arabic in public has become a real issue in Israel. It’s the subject of panel debates on television, where speakers compete to express increasingly extreme views and to incite against Palestinian doctors, bus drivers and students.
A woman in the mixed Arab city of Yaffa told me she was afraid to use public transport in her town, fearing she would be attacked by Israeli groups.
This past summer, three Arab female employees were dismissed from a fashion store in Afula after refusing to comply with a branch manager’s ban on speaking Arabic at work.
Hate speech and racism dominate Israeli public life to a degree I have never witnessed before. Attacks by Israeli Jewish groups on Palestinians who speak Arabic, or on women who wear headscarves in the street, have become routine.
But the hatred is not directed solely at Palestinians. Secular Israelis attack Haredim, or ultra-Orthodox Jews, for not serving in the army; the Haredim attack coffee shops that open on Shabbat.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump lands in China for meeting with Xi and Putin
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
Trump lands in China for meeting with Xi and Putin
US President Donald Trump has arrived in China for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladmir Putin.
The historic trilateral meeting between the leaders will take place on Thursday. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet on the sidelines of the summit to potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran, as well as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.
Xi met Trump off the plane on the tarmac at Shenzhen, reciprocating Trump's gesture when the Chinese leader visited the US in September.
Xi told Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Putin and Trump are unlikely to have time for fully fledged bilateral negotiations in China, but may talk on the event's sidelines, the Tass news agency reported.
Peskov was cited as saying that the two leaders would exchange views on the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran if they got a chance to talk one-on-one.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump's Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire has delivered 'nothing visible'
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
Trump's Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire has delivered 'nothing visible'
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace, the body supposedly tasked with overseeing the end to fighting in Gaza, has accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to end hostilities, leaving the Palestinian enclave's population in dire need.
The 12-page Board of Peace report, seen by Reuters, is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the US-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a "sobering assessment of progress made since then", Reuters said.
The board, established and headed by Trump, is expected to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November.
“The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” the report said, warning that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely.”
Since the ceasefire, Israeli attacks have killed more than 1,431 people, including at least 300 children, and wounded 5,026.
The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a spokesperson for the political office of Hamas did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the report.
“There is no ceasefire in Gaza. People talk about a ceasefire but at best it’s a reduced fire,” Chris Sidoti, a member of the UN Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told MEE's Expert Witness podcast this week.

Tanks advance near Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps, forcing displaced Palestinian families to flee as at least two people are wounded by indiscriminate fire
This picture taken from a position in the Upper Galilee in northern Israel shows an Israeli army tank being positioned along the Israel-Lebanon border, on 1 July 2026 (Jack Guez/AFP)
Off
The Israeli military launched a new ground assault on residential areas in the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, forcing displaced Palestinian families to flee despite the ceasefire agreement.
Tanks were seen advancing into areas near the Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps, according to local media.
At least two people were wounded by indiscriminate fire near Nuseirat refugee camp, while scores of residents fled the area following the surprise assault.
The Israeli military confirmed the attack, which is taking place beyond the so-called 'Yellow Line' – a military boundary imposed by Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip following the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
The army claimed it was targeting "terrorist infrastructure" in areas it designated as “Blocks 660, 661 and 666”. These are residential areas where Palestinian residents and displaced families live.
It urged people to "stay away" from its troops, despite issuing no advance warning of the assault.
The military also confirmed that Salah al-Din Road, one of the two main routes connecting northern and southern Gaza, would be closed in the targeted area.
Hamas condemned the assault and held Israel and the United States responsible.

data.title: Middle East Eye: India signs $211m contract with Israel Aerospace Industries
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
India signs $211m contract with Israel Aerospace Industries
India has signed a contract worth 19.76bn rupees ($211.48m) with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of Barak Point Defence Missile System for the Indian navy, the Indian defence ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
Israel Aerospace Industries is Israel's largest state-owned aerospace and defence manufacturer. The company makes multiple weapons systems specifically for the Israeli military, including the Heron TP killer drone.
Its CEO, Boaz Levy, has said that Heron drones have “played a pivotal role” in Israel’s attacks on Gaza, including in strike operations.
The Barak Point Defence Missile System is marketed as a "combat proven" defence "against drones, aircraft, cruise missiles and tactical ballistic missiles".

Israel kills three Palestinians, including a child, in attacks across Gaza

The deaths follow six fatalities on Tuesday, including that of a six-year-old boy
A mourner during the funeral of Palestinians who were killed in an Israeli strike at Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, 11 November 2026 (Mahmoud Issa/Reuters)
Off
Three Palestinians, including a child, have been killed following Israeli attacks in northern and central Gaza on Wednesday, Palestinian media reported.
According to the Arab48 news site, 11-year-old Mansour Khader Nabhan succumbed to wounds sustained in an Israeli attack on the Bir al-Na’ja area in northern Gaza a day earlier.
The outlet added that a young man - Thaer al-Wadiya - was killed in a drone strike in the Sheikh Ajlin neighbourhood, southwest of Gaza City. It noted that three of al-Wadiya's brothers had already been killed in Israeli attacks.
Meanwhile, Wafa news agency reported that 35-year-old Fadi Nahid Rajab Ismail was killed in a separate attack in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah.
The latest fatalities follow six deaths, including that of a six-year-old, in Israeli attacks across the Strip on Tuesday.
According to medics cited by Reuters, two people, including six-year-old Eyas al-Nimnim, were killed in separate Israeli attacks in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah. Al Jazeera said that the child was shot in the head while sheltering in his tent east of Deir al-Balah.
It added that a Palestinian man was also shot dead by Israeli fire in the city's east, while a drone strike in Khan Younis killed a 50-year-old man and another in Beit Lahiya killed one person and seriously wounded a child.
In Rafah, another man was shot dead by Israeli forces, while a sixth Palestinian succumbed to wounds sustained in an Israeli attack on a school in northern Gaza two weeks ago.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Somalia's president accuses UAE of 'interference' in the country
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Somalia's president accuses UAE of 'interference' in the country
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/18/2026 - 10:19
Hassan Sheikh Mohamud says Gulf state has funded armed groups and established bases in breakaway Somaliland
President of Somalia Hassan Sheikh Mohamud addresses the 81st session of the United Nations (UN) General Assembly in New York City on 24 September (AFP/Alexi J. Rosenfeld)
Off
The president of Somalia has accused the UAE of "interference" in his country's internal affairs.
Speaking in a televised address, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said the UAE had established a military presence, including bases, outside Mogadishu’s national security framework without the government's approval.
He said the country had also funded armed groups and opponents of the central government.
"Somalia is not a thoroughfare to be traversed illegally - it is not a commodity to be bought, nor is it a place that one can enter or leave at will," Hassan Sheikh said.
Tensions between the UAE and Somalia have been high for many years, in part due to the former's support for the breakaway nation of Somaliland.
Mogadishu annulled all agreements with the UAE earlier this year and closed its airspace to Emirati military and cargo aircraft.
Israel's first ambassador to Somaliland has credentials accepted
Read More »
It has accused the Gulf state of signing deals at the ports of Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo without government approval.
It also says the UAE played a role in Israel becoming the first country in the world to recognise Somaliland.
Israel recognised Somaliland in January and is eyeing a military base in the port of Berbera alongside the UAE.
DP World, the Emirati logistics company, runs the main port there, as part of a partnership with the British government’s foreign investment arm.
Somaliland declared its independence in 1991 after a decade of war, escaping the civil war and instability that later engulfed Somalia.
